old_caption: The video captures a sequence set outdoors on a grassy area with bushes in the background. The scene is dominated by a large, multi-tiered structure made of cardboard boxes. A small, round object, possibly a marble, is seen rolling down the sloped surface of the cardboard structure. As it descends, it approaches a metallic pot placed at the bottom of the slope. The pot is positioned on top of another cardboard box, and next to it lies a pink plastic container with a lid. The marble continues its descent, eventually reaching the pot but does not cause it to tip over. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing on the action as the marble rolls down the slope and interacts with the pot. The overall setting suggests a controlled environment designed to observe the effects of gravity and momentum.
original_wisa_caption: The video captures a sequence of events set outdoors on a grassy area with some bushes in the background. The scene is dominated by a large, multi-tiered structure made of cardboard boxes, which appears to be part of an elaborate setup for a physics experiment or demonstration. A small, round object, possibly a marble or ball, is seen rolling down the sloped surface of the cardboard structure. As it descends, it approaches a metallic pot placed at the bottom of the slope. The pot is positioned on top of another cardboard box, and next to it lies a pink plastic container with a lid. The marble continues its descent, eventually reaching the pot and causing it to tip over slightly. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing on the action as the marble rolls down the slope and interacts with the pot. The overall setting suggests a controlled environment designed to observe the effects of gravity and momentum.
caption: The video captures an outdoor lawn where stacked brown cardboard boxes form a staircase ramp on wooden blocks at the left, beside an upside-down metal pot, a pink lid, a metal bowl, and a pale tray at the right. A small shiny blue marble rolls down the stepped cardboard surface, dropping from one raised edge to the next as it descends. It reaches the flat top of the lowest box and travels across that smooth surface, angling toward the metal pot. The marble slips off the box edge and lands on the curved lid of the upside-down pot. On the lid it keeps moving, crossing from the left side toward the center-right while the pot stays fixed. Near the top a second, darker spherical object appears and begins rolling down the steps while the blue marble is already on the pot. The background yellow sack, vertical post, and box structure stay in place. Green and blue glints shift across the marble with its motion, reflecting light rather than marking a new object.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.

collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.

camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.
Do not shorten a rich caption into a terse technical checklist. Avoid annotation phrases such as
'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.
